description: Radio Array Explorer reference catalogue. Edit this file, not generated exports.

methods.station_coordinates: Rounded planning coordinates; no local horizon masks or observatory scheduling limits.
methods.visibility: Continuous common window above elevation threshold; repeating sidereal-day geometry, not a dated schedule.
methods.sensitivity: Representative band reference; thermal-equivalent t^-1/2 scaling only; calibration/confusion not modelled.

facilities.name: Allen Telescope Array (ATA)

sensitivity.reference: ~3 GHz; 28 active antennas; 672 MHz; two polarizations; thermal estimate from 272–291 Jy array SEFD; not measured image rms
sensitivity.calculation: Mean array SEFD 281.5 Jy / sqrt(2 * 672 MHz * 3600 s) * sqrt(28/27); ideal cross-correlation correction; no calibration, RFI or confusion losses.

warnings: Uses the 28 active, upgraded antennas reported in October 2026, from 42 installed. Backend/antenna availability for a particular imaging campaign must be checked.

The 1–10 GHz active range is divided into L (1–2), S (2–4), C (4–8) and truncated X (8–10) GHz intervals for display; these are not separate receivers. Arithmetic midpoints are plotted. Broader advertised feed coverage is not assumed here.
Nominal angular scale uses lambda / 300 m in radians. This is a baseline-based planning estimate, not a measured or projected synthesized FWHM; the elongated array gives an elliptical beam.

Sensitivity is a provisional ideal continuum imaging estimate from the published beamformed-array SEFD, using one 672 MHz tuning and two polarizations. It is not an achieved imaging rms or a SETI narrowband detection threshold.
Visibility uses the existing geometric elevation test at Hat Creek; local horizon masks and the 87-degree mechanical zenith limit are not modelled.
facilities.provenance: Added 2026-11-05. Current active array/range/SEFD: Gerrard & Sheikh (2026), arXiv:2610.07065, sections 1.3, 2.1 and Table 2. Baseline and coordinates: ATA Interface Document v1.2 (2020).

facilities.name: FAST Core Array

sensitivity.reference: 1.4 GHz; design Aeff/Tsys ≈3000 m²/K; assumed 400 MHz continuum bandwidth, two polarizations; ideal thermal estimate
sensitivity.calculation: SEFD = 2 kB / (Aeff/Tsys) = 0.9204 Jy; rms = SEFD / sqrt(2 * 400 MHz * 3600 s). The 400 MHz usable bandwidth and unit efficiency are adopted planning assumptions, not a quoted achieved image rms.

warnings: Proposed full FAST Core Array from Jiang et al. (2024): one FAST telescope plus 24 new 40-m dishes. The six-dish precursor and larger FASTA concept are not this row.

The three receiver ranges are taken from Table 3. Markers use arithmetic midpoints 0.70, 2.20 and 6.65 GHz. Resolution scales as 1/frequency from Table 1: 4.3 arcsec at 1.4 GHz; these are nominal design scales, not projected beams.
FAST sets a 50-degree minimum elevation in section 2.2. The greater of this limit and the user-selected minimum is used for continuous visibility.

The ~3000 m²/K sensitivity is specified only at 1.4 GHz. The ~0.54 µJy/beam one-hour reference assumes 400 MHz usable bandwidth and two polarizations, with no weighting, calibration or confusion losses; it is a provisional design estimate.

Full-array antenna count is an image-quality proxy. Table 3 specifies the secondary-dish feeds; FAST receiver availability and full-array participation across the whole proposed range require confirmation, particularly at high frequencies. A proposed FAST PAF covers 1–3 GHz.
facilities.provenance: Added 2026-11-05 from user-provided FASTarray.pdf: Jiang et al. (2024), The FAST Core Array, DOI 10.61977/ati2024012; section 2.2, Tables 1–3, and section 3.3. Site coordinates rounded for planning.

facilities.name: EHT

sensitivity.reference: No comparable one-hour imaging rms adopted; requires band, station and weather assumptions.

warnings: Optional facility: excluded from all default comparisons and from initial detailed selections. Select explicitly to include.

Rounded illustrative station roster, not a guaranteed observing allocation. Phased arrays count as single VLBI stations in N². Weather, phasing, fringe-detection limits and observing seasons are not simulated.

At a chosen declination, at least three stations must share one continuous hour above the elevation limit. Reduced-subset angular scales use physical baseline-extent ratios, not projected beam synthesis.

230 GHz marker is a nominal ~25 microarcsecond fringe spacing; 345 GHz is the demonstrated ~19 microarcsecond fringe spacing, not an assertion of routine full-array imaging. The 345 GHz mode uses only the six sites in the published demonstration.
N² and station list describe the lowest-frequency displayed band with an accepted common visibility window. Other bands may use fewer stations; marker tooltips show their counts.
Sensitivity is not estimated: narrowband fringe detection and published reconstructed-image noise are not interchangeable with a one-hour image rms.
facilities.provenance: Added 2026-11-05 using EHT station list, ITU-R RA.2508-0 and EHT Collaboration first 870-micron detections (2024). Rounded planning coordinates.

facilities.name: GMVA

sensitivity.reference: 86 GHz; Europe + VLBA + GBT + phased ALMA; published ideal 1h array rms, 512 MHz; not the full illustrative roster.

warnings: Optional facility: excluded from all default comparisons and from initial detailed selections. Select explicitly to include.

Rounded illustrative station roster, not a guaranteed observing allocation. Phased arrays count as single VLBI stations in N². Weather, phasing, fringe-detection limits and observing seasons are not simulated.

At a chosen declination, at least three stations must share one continuous hour above the elevation limit. Reduced-subset angular scales use physical baseline-extent ratios, not projected beam synthesis.
The marker uses 87 GHz, the midpoint of the documented 84–90 GHz common tuning range. The usual continuum setup is near 86 GHz; the nominal 45 microarcsecond reference is scaled by 86/87.
Illustrative roster includes optional/best-effort ALMA, APEX, LMT and GLT, plus four KVN stations. Participation requires campaign-specific proposals and availability checks.

Published 29 µJy/beam 1h reference applies to Europe + VLBA + GBT + ALMA under ideal conditions, not every station listed here. The reference is left unestimated whenever visibility removes stations. Typical duty cycle is ~0.5, so 1h on source needs ~2h scheduled.
facilities.provenance: Added 2026-11-05 from MPIfR GMVA technical/sensitivity pages and NRAO 2026B GMVA status. Rounded planning coordinates.

facilities.name: WSRT (Westerbork)

sensitivity.reference: Apertif DR1 ~1.36 GHz; 36.1 µJy/beam outer-image median in 11.5 h, scaled to 1 h; historical achieved reference

warnings: Real existing facility; this row uses the documented Apertif imaging reference. ASTRON describes Apertif survey operations as concluded after 2019–2022. Current observing availability must be checked; real does not guarantee this imaging mode can be scheduled.
Apertif uses 12 of 14 installed 25-m dishes, so the image-quality proxy uses N=12. Older multi-frequency WSRT receiver modes are not assumed to remain available.
1.44 GHz is the arithmetic midpoint of the Apertif tunable range 1.13–1.75 GHz; only 300 MHz is processed at once. Nominal minor-axis beam is scaled from the survey reference 15 arcsec at 1.28 GHz.

The east-west array produces an elliptical beam, approximately theta_minor by theta_minor/abs(sin(declination)); only its nominal minor-axis scale is plotted. Near the celestial equator the beam becomes highly elongated. No projected beam calculation is performed.
Sensitivity is a historical DR1 reference, scaled with sqrt(time). It is not an achieved one-hour observation, and calibration, RFI, field position and weighting affect actual rms.
facilities.provenance: Added 2026-11-05 from ASTRON Apertif system overview, survey and DR1 documentation. Rounded WSRT site coordinates; nominal survey-beam scaling and achieved-noise exposure scaling.

facilities.name: GMRT (uGMRT)

sensitivity.reference: 700 MHz (Band 4); Tsys=100 K, gain=0.35 K/Jy, 30 antennas, 200 MHz, two polarizations; ideal thermal estimate with assumed efficiency 0.9
sensitivity.calculation: SEFD=Tsys/gain=285.7 Jy; image rms=SEFD / [0.9 sqrt(2 N(N-1) bandwidth time)]. Unit setup: 30 antennas, 200 MHz usable bandwidth, 3600 s. No RFI/calibration/confusion losses.

warnings: Full upgraded GMRT reference: 30 antennas, not a guaranteed nightly count. The observatory targets at least 26 available antennas during maintenance.

Band ranges use the current status-document overview: 120–250, 250–500, 550–850 and 1000–1460 MHz, with arithmetic midpoints 185, 375, 700 and 1230 MHz. Table 1 starts Band 2 at 125 MHz; its 17.3 arcsec beam at 187.5 MHz is scaled to 185 MHz here.

Nominal whole-array synthesized beams come from Table 1 of the status document. Actual beam shape depends on declination, available baselines and weighting. The compact central square is not a separate physically reconfigured array row.

Sensitivity is an ideal one-hour continuum estimate, not the deepest achieved rms values in Table 1, whose integration times are unspecified. Band-4 gain and Tsys are from Table 1; 200 MHz usable bandwidth, dual polarization and 0.9 efficiency are explicit assumptions.
The 17-degree software elevation limit is enforced when it exceeds the user-selected minimum.
facilities.provenance: Added 2026-11-05 using NCRA GMRT System Parameters and Current Status dated 15 December 2025, overview and Table 1, plus the official antenna specification page. Rounded planning site coordinates.
